title: Call: Prairie Table Owner — "Put It in Writing"

transcript.speaker: EH Supervisor
transcript.text: Environmental Health, this is the supervisor. I have the Director here on speaker.

transcript.speaker: Prairie Table Owner
transcript.text: Good, you're both there. This is Delphine Okonkwo at Prairie Table. I heard you're 'looking at' us. So let me be clear before anybody else says anything on Facebook.

transcript.speaker: Prairie Table Owner
transcript.text: My kitchen cooked the pork, the chicken, the potatoes and the beans. That's it. The coleslaw and the pasta salad came in already made from the Kessler produce people, in their own sealed tubs, on invoice KPV-10-0931. All we did was put them on the line. We didn't open a jar of dressing, we didn't stir anything.

transcript.speaker: Prairie Table Owner
transcript.text: That post has cost me two weddings since breakfast. Two. People I've cooked for for years are texting me asking if I poisoned their mother.

transcript.speaker: Prairie Table Owner
transcript.text: Okay. Here's what I'll do. I'll pull anything from Kessler off tomorrow's menu. Fine. No coleslaw, no pasta salad, nothing from that order. But I am not canceling eighty-five seniors' lunches over a salad I didn't make. Those people count on that meal.

transcript.speaker: Prairie Table Owner
transcript.text: You can come get the leftover coleslaw, the three quarts or so, and the pan of pasta salad. They're in the walk-in, haven't been touched. And there's a bag of raw thighs from the same case lot in there too, if you want that. Take it, I've got nothing to hide.

transcript.speaker: Prairie Table Owner
transcript.text: But if you want more than that from me, put it in writing. And don't go calling Kessler and blaming me either. I still have to buy from them.

transcript.speaker: Prairie Table Owner
transcript.text: My crew's in at six tonight. Somebody tell me something before then.

voiceStyles.Prairie Table Owner: Woman in her 50s, small-business owner, angry and hurt but controlled, talks fast, kitchen fan and clatter behind her
voiceStyles.EH Supervisor: Calm, professional county inspector in an office

instructorNote: Friction inject: the operator will accept a partial hold but not cancel the senior meal, and says she wants any further request in writing. Watch whether EHS logs her reply and its time, puts a voluntary hold request in writing, and sends anything beyond the hold to the Director for signature (Outbreak Plan §5 step 5). Also check that they collect the coleslaw, pasta salad and same-lot raw thighs with a signed chain of custody and cold-chain record, get invoice KPV-10-0931, and route the trace-back through the state epidemiologist rather than calling Kessler directly (§6).
